messages.text: Finally had a chance to plug in my nerdQoctaxe++ - and it does not work.  The fans try to spin but only move about 3 cm then stop.  It’s not working…..
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Hi, I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sorry it's not running after all that waiting. Let's find out why.

When fans twitch a few centimetres and then stop, it usually means the unit isn't getting enough power at startup. The power brick is often the cause, not the miner. To narrow it down, two quick questions:

1. Does the little screen on the front light up or show anything, even for a second?
2. Which power supply are you using: the one that came in the box, or another one? If you can, send a photo of its label so I can see the voltage and amps.

While you check, plug the brick straight into a wall socket, not a power strip or extension. Make sure the round barrel plug is pushed fully into the miner.
Nothing on the screen and it came with a nice PSU unit with it

Thanks. A blank screen plus fans that twitch and stop means the power is cutting out almost straight away. That points to either the power supply or the miner's board, and the next check will tell us which.

1. Unplug the miner from the power supply and wait about 30 seconds.
2. Plug the power supply into a different wall socket. Before you connect the miner, look for a small light on the brick. Is it on, and is it steady?
3. Now connect the miner and watch that light while the fans twitch. Does it stay steady, blink, or go out?

If you can, record a short phone video of step 3 showing both the brick's light and the fans, and send it here. That video tells us more than anything else at this point.

Also, if you have another power supply with the same voltage and connector, like one from another miner, tell me before you try it. I'll check it's safe for this unit first.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks for the photo. It shows the label of a Mean Well LRS-350-12. That's a solid 12 V, 29 A (350 W) supply, plenty for this miner, so the brick's size isn't the issue.

The yellow sticker is the important part. It's in Chinese, and it warns you to set the input voltage switch correctly before powering on: the 115V position for 110 V mains, the 230V position for 220 V mains. On the wrong setting the supply can't power the miner properly, and fans twitching then stopping is a classic sign of that.

1. **Unplug the power supply from the wall first.**
2. Find the small slide switch on the side of the supply, near the screw terminals. It's marked 115V / 230V. Don't touch the screw terminals.
3. Tell me where it's set and what country you're in (or your wall voltage).

What to do next depends on the answer:
- **Switch on 230V and you're on 110 to 120 V mains** (US, Canada): with it unplugged, slide it to 115V, then plug back in and try the miner.
- **Switch on 115V and you're on 220 to 240 V mains** (UK, EU, Australia): do not plug it in again. Tell me, and we'll take it from there.
- **Switch already matches your mains:** tell me that too, and we'll move to the next check.
The red switch is set to 115

Thanks, 115 is the right setting for 110 to 120 V mains, so I just need one more fact: **what country are you in?** (or what voltage are your wall sockets?)

- **US, Canada or another 110 to 120 V country:** the switch is correct and the supply isn't the problem. We'll move on to the next check.
- **UK, Europe, Australia or another 220 to 240 V country:** leave the supply unplugged and don't try it again. Running a 115V setting on 230 V mains can damage it.

Until you reply, keep it unplugged to be safe.
Canada

Thanks. Canada is 120 V, so the 115 setting is correct. The supply is set up right, so let's check whether it's actually putting out power.

1. Plug the supply into the wall with the miner **disconnected**.
2. Look near the screw terminals for a small **green light** on the supply. Don't touch the terminals. Is it on?
3. Connect the miner and watch that green light while the fans twitch. Does it stay on, flicker, or go out?

While it's unplugged, also make sure the cable from the supply is pushed fully into the miner. A plug that's only half in can cause exactly this twitch-and-stop behaviour.

If you can, take a short video of step 3 showing the green light and the fans together. It's the clearest way to tell whether the supply or the miner is cutting out.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks for the photo. It shows the top of the miner: the red control board, the LILYGO screen (blank, so the unit is unpowered or off here), the power jack at the top left, the fan cable plugged into its header, and the Thermalright fan on the heatsink. From this angle I can't see any scorch marks, swollen cap···· anything loose. That's good news.

Two quick checks:

1. **The green light on the power supply:** with it plugged into the wall, is the small green light near its terminals on? (Miner disconnected for this one.)
2. **Reseat the screen:** that LILYGO screen module is also the miner's brain, and it plugs into the board on pins. A knock in shipping can lift it slightly, and then the board gets power but never starts. That would match your twitch-and-stop fans. With everything **unplugged**, press gently and evenly on the screen's clear case so it sits flat on its pins, then reconnect and power up.

Let me know what the green light does and whether the screen comes on after the reseat.
The light is green on the PSU without the miner plugged in….let me try the next atep

Good, a steady green light with nothing connected means the supply is alive and putting out 12 V. Go ahead with the screen reseat.

When you power up after the reseat, watch the green light on the supply too:

- **Screen comes on:** great, that was it.
- **Fans twitch again and the green light flickers or goes out:** the miner is pulling the supply down, which points to the board.
- **Fans twitch again and the green light stays steady:** the supply is fine and the miner isn't starting on its own.

Tell me which one you see.
PSU light turned off

That's a useful result, though not the one we wanted. The supply works with nothing connected, but its light goes out as soon as the miner is attached. That means the supply is shutting itself off to protect itself, because the miner is drawing far too much current the moment it powers up. A 350 W Mean Well has plenty of power for this miner, so that usually means a short, either in the power cable or on the board.

**Please stop powering it for now.** Repeated power-ups into a short can make things worse.

With everything unplugged, three last checks:

1. **Look and smell:** any burning smell, or any dark or melted spot on the board, especially near the power jack and the three square black parts in the middle? If you smell burning, leave it unplugged.
2. **Check the cable** that runs from the supply to the miner. Look for a pinched, cut or melted section, and check that the plug end isn't bent or damaged.
3. **Send me a short video** of one power-up showing the green light and the fans together, plus a **clear photo of the serial number sticker** on the miner. Only do the power-up for the video if steps 1 and 2 looked clean.

If the cable looks fine, the video and serial photo are what's needed to assess this properly, so please send them here.
Green light flickers every time the fans twitch
Handed to the team · Needs JD's call: likely shorted board vs cable. Checks done: PSU label and volta

That confirms it. The light flickers in time with each fan twitch because the supply cuts out the moment the miner draws power, recovers, then cuts out again. Your power supply is fine. Something on the miner side, either the cable or the board, is pulling far too much current at power-up. A setting can't fix that, so please **leave it unplugged** from now on.

I've passed everything we found to JD, our hardware lead. The team is offline for the weekend and picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer will come to your email.

To give JD the full picture, you can still send these here whenever you have them:
1. Whether the power cable looked damaged (pinched, cut, melted, bent plug) and whether there was any burning smell.
2. A photo of the serial number sticker on the miner.
3. The short video you may already have of the light flickering with the fans.

If you'd like a faster answer over the weekend, our Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Post there and mention **@nullhashrate** (that's JD).

Thanks for being so patient while we ran those checks.
Not able to send videos in this chat

No problem, the video isn't essential. You've already told me exactly what it would show: the green light flickers off with each fan twitch. That's in the notes I passed to JD.

If you'd still like JD to see it, you can post the video on our Discord (https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf), which takes videos, and mention **@nullhashrate**.

Photos do work here, so whenever you can, please send:
1. A photo of the **serial number sticker** on the miner.
2. A word on the **power cable**: any damage, and any burning smell?

Until then, keep the miner unplugged.
The PSU red/black cables are actually twitching when the fans twitch too

Thanks, that's a telling detail. When the red and black cables physically jump with each pulse, very large bursts of current are flowing through them. That fits a hard short on the miner side, not a weak supply. This chat, including that detail, stays with your case for JD.

For safety, from here on:

1. **Unplug the power supply from the wall** and leave it unplugged. Don't power the miner up again, not even for a video.
2. Don't touch the screw terminals or the red and black wires while the supply is plugged in.
3. Once it's been unplugged for a few minutes, carefully check whether the wires, the plug at the miner, or the power jack feel warm, or whether anything smells burnt. Let me know either way.

That's all the testing we need. JD will have the full picture Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email. When you have a moment, please also send the serial number photo.
There is also a little pop and spark of light when the yellow connected begins to plug into the unit.
Handed to the team · Spark/pop reported, safety rule: customer told to unplug at the wall and stop po

Thanks for telling me. A pop and a spark settle it: **please stop all testing now.**

1. **Unplug the power supply from the wall**, and leave the yellow connector disconnected from the miner.
2. Don't plug it in again, not even to check or film it.
3. Keep the miner and supply somewhere dry, away from anything flammable, until this is sorted.

A tiny spark from a yellow connector can sometimes just be the miner's cap····charging. But with the supply cutting out and the cables jumping too, it fits a short on the miner side. That isn't something you should keep testing at home.

I've added the pop and spark to your case for JD. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email. When you get a chance, a photo of the miner's serial number sticker here would help.

For something sooner over the weekend, you can post on the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention **@nullhashrate** (JD).
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that's the photo I needed. The label reads:

- **Model:** NerdQaxe 12T
- **Power input:** 12 V via XT60, the yellow connector you mentioned
- **Serial:** (number hidden). The last few digits are a little faint, so please tell me if any differ on the sticker.

It's all in this chat, so JD has it alongside everything else when the team picks it up Monday at 10am ET. The answer comes to your email.

One last thing whenever you're ready: after a few minutes unplugged, do the yellow connector, the red and black wires, or the miner's power socket look scorched or feel warm, and is there any burning smell? Keep the supply unplugged from the wall in the meantime.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks. The photo shows the black power lead printed **"12AWG 200°C"**, with the red lead beside it. That's thick, high-temperature silicone wire, more than heavy enough for this miner, and the section you've shown looks clean, with no cuts, melting or scorching. So the wire itself isn't too thin.

What's left is the two ends, where a short or the spark you saw would leave marks:

1. **The yellow XT60 plug:** look into it and at the miner's matching socket. Are the metal pins blackened, pitted or bent? Is any yellow plastic melted?
2. **Any warmth or burning smell** at either end?

A photo of the XT60 plug and the miner's socket, looking straight in, would help most. Keep the supply unplugged from the wall while you look.
Thank you - do you need anything else from me?

No, you've given me everything that matters. Thanks for working through all of that so carefully.

Here's what your case has for JD:
- **Unit:** NerdQaxe 12T, serial (number hidden), 12 V XT60 input
- **Supply:** Mean Well LRS-350-12, set to 115V (correct for Canada), steady green light with nothing connected
- **Fault:** blank screen, fans twitch and stop, the supply's light flickers with each twitch, the cables jump, and the XT60 pops and sparks when plugged in
- **Already ruled out:** wrong voltage setting, a loose screen module, and wire thickness (12 AWG, clean)

The one optional extra is a straight-on photo of the yellow XT60 plug and the miner's socket, if you get a chance. Send it here whenever you like.

Until then, keep the supply unplugged from the wall and don't power the miner up again. The team picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email. If you'd like quicker input over the weekend, post on the Discord (https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf) and mention **@nullhashrate**.
There is not burning, bending or anything on the yellow connector of the PSU or the miner - just golden colour.

That's good to hear. Clean gold pins on both sides mean the connectors and cable are fine. With the supply, the voltage setting, the wire and both plugs all checked, the problem points to the miner's board itself, which is what JD will look at.

You've done every check there is to do, so there's nothing more you need to send. Keep the supply unplugged from the wall and leave the miner disconnected. The team picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email.

Thanks again for being so thorough. Have a good weekend.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that confirms it. The photo shows the yellow XT60 plug on the power supply's lead, looking straight in. Both gold sockets are clean and shiny, with no blackening or pitting, and the yellow plastic isn't melted or warped. The Mean Well is behind it.

So the connector is ruled out too, and everything on the power side checks out. That photo is now with the rest of your case for JD.

There's nothing else you need to do. Keep the supply unplugged from the wall and the miner disconnected. The team picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks. This one shows the miner's own XT60 socket on the edge of the board. Both gold pins look clean and straight, with no blackening, pitting or melted plastic around them. The fan cables and braided leads around it look fine too.

That means everything you can check from the outside is clean on both ends. Whatever is drawing too much current is inside the miner, past the connector, which is a job for JD, not something to keep testing at home.

You're all set. Keep everything unplugged. The team picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email.
Fuse is fully in tact too

Good to know, thanks. The green part next to the XT60 socket in your last photo looks like that fuse, and it does look intact. That fits what we've seen: the supply cuts itself off within a split second, before enough current flows to blow the fuse. So an intact fuse doesn't rule out a fault further inside the board.

Please leave the fuse where it is. Don't pull it out or swap it.

That's everything noted for JD. Keep it all unplugged. The team picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email.
Okay thank you I look forward to getting this fixed

You're welcome, and thanks for being so patient. Every check you ran is noted, so JD gets a clear picture without having to ask you to repeat anything.

The team picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email. Until then, keep it all unplugged. If you want to chat with JD or the community over the weekend, the Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf (mention **@nullhashrate**).

Have a good weekend.
Thanks
Anytime. Take care, and enjoy your weekend.
You as well!
Thank you! Talk soon.
